text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed nearly 10% over two weeks, with today's modest gain continuing that streak. The rally is driven by a sharp rise in global crude oil prices—world oil is trading at $130.80 per barrel, up significantly from typical levels—fueled by escalating Middle East tensions. Iran's threats of retaliation against Trump administration pressure, combined with Houthi attacks on shipping and closure of the Strait of Hormuz, have created supply-chain anxiety that pushes crude prices higher and widens refinery profit margins.

Refineries are running at 96.8% capacity while global crude supplies tighten, which means Marathon's plants are operating near full throttle at a time when they can earn more from each barrel they process—the gap between crude costs and refined product prices widens when crude gets expensive and scarce. This is the sweet spot for refiners, and the market is pricing in sustained geopolitical risk keeping oil elevated.
